samples.summary: New spill handling when clearing destination cells under a moved merge has no test
samples.evidence: The delta adds a substantial new branch inside the moved-merge destination-clearing loop: skip ghost cells (`cell.spillAnchor`), delete a spill anchor's ghosts plus `clearSpillBlockers` before clearing it, and `clearSpillBlockers` for a `spillBlocked` cell (sheet.ts ~2398-2417). The only tests added in merge.test.ts are 'should persist the propagated merge to the store' and 'should recalculate dependants of a merge the move removed'; neither creates a spill (array-formula) cell anywhere near the destination, so none of these three code paths is exercised. If the ghost-orphaning or blocker cleanup were wrong, every test in packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts would still pass. Spill behavior is clearly testable in this suite (spill cases exist in packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts).

samples.evidence: The delta also adds `changedSrefs.add(sref)` for every cell newly covered by the propagated merge at the destination (sheet.ts:2391), so that formulas reading a previously empty destination cell recalculate once it starts aliasing the new anchor. finding.summary: No test asserts merge propagation is persisted to the store; all assertions read the in-memory map
finding.evidence: Every new test asserts via `sheet.getMerges()` (merge.test.ts:107, 137, 182, 206, 225), which is the sync accessor returning `this.merges` directly (sheet.ts:763-765). The new code additionally calls `await this.store.deleteMerge(...)` and `await this.store.setMerge(...)` (sheet.ts:2366, 2375) — the persistence half of the change. If both store calls were deleted, all six tests would still pass, yet the merge would be lost on reload/collaboration. `Store.getMerges()` is available and async (memory.ts:467) and `Sheet.load` reads from it (sheet.ts:497), so a `await store.getMerges()` assertion is easy and absent.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test asserts merge propagation is persisted to the store. A dedicated test exists: merge.test.ts:143-164 'should persist the propagated merge to the store' creates the MemStore explicitly, performs moveRangeTo on a merged range, then asserts `const stored = await store.getMerges()` (line 160) with `stored.size === 1` (161), `stored.get('A3')` equals the span (162), and `stored.has('A1') === false` (163). Those assertions read the store's own map, which MemStore keeps separately from Sheet.merges (memory.ts:459-469, getMerges returns `new Map(this.merges)`; Sheet only copies from it at sheet.ts:497). Removing `store.setMerge` (sheet.ts:2382) would fail lines 161-162, and removing `store.deleteMerge` (sheet.ts:2373) would fail lines 161 and 163 — so the finding's mutation claim ('if both store calls were deleted, all tests still pass') is concretely false. The reviewer's cited grep result is inconsistent with the working tree, which contains store.getMerges() at merge.test.ts:160.
